description: dryvist/.github master Renovate preset — the single source of truth for Renovate policy across ALL dryvist AND JacobPEvans repos. This is the MASTER: it extends no other repository’s config. JacobPEvans/.github extends THIS (github>dryvist/.github:renovate-presets), never the reverse. Consumers extend it via local>dryvist/.github (the default preset, which extends this) or directly via github>dryvist/.github:renovate-presets.

Architecture: this file holds global policy (auto-merge, trusted orgs, stability features, custom managers). Ecosystem grouping rules live in renovate-grouping.json and are pulled in via extends below. Inline description fields on each rule are the canonical documentation — keep them current.

WARNING: platformAutomerge MUST stay false. GitHub’s auto-merge queue has a known bug where PRs pass all checks but GitHub never executes the merge — PRs stall for days with no error. With false, Renovate merges directly via API with built-in retry logic. Do NOT set this to true.

Tiered freshness model (canonical: SECURITY.md → Dependency Trust, and docs.jacobpevans.com/infrastructure/cicd/dependency-automation). MINOR/PATCH updates auto-merge PUBLISHER-AGNOSTICALLY — any package, any ecosystem (dryvist/** auto-merges patch, minor and major) — after a 3-day release-age stabilization + green CI (the Merge Gate, plus the deterministic dependency-review supply-chain scan on public repos). Lock-file maintenance cannot use Renovate's minimumReleaseAge because a package manager selects every changed version. Instead, Renovate creates the branch only in one of two fixed source windows and considers automerge only in a later fixed window at least 72 elapsed hours away; the branch is never refreshed outside its source window, so the policy is a real current-head soak without custom automation. The four-hour windows preserve the existing Monday 05:00 and Thursday 13:00 starts while matching Renovate's hosted scheduler guidance, preventing a once-per-four-hours scheduler from missing either run. Trust tiers gate ONLY majors and PR-creation cadence, never minor/patch. PR-creation cadence: every non-daily tier (top-level default, the broad minor/patch rule, the trusted-org major rule, custom-regex managers, lockFileMaintenance) runs on exactly two weekly windows — Monday early morning and Thursday afternoon America/New_York; first-party (own-org) overrides to 'at any time' for immediate propagation, and repos with a genuinely daily cadence (e.g. nix-darwin's flake-input groups) keep that cadence locally rather than adopting the two-window default. MAJORS never auto-merge (a compatible-looking version is not a compatible API): JacobPEvans majors auto-merge immediately, dryvist majors auto-merge after green CI (except on automerge-manual repos), trusted-org majors open a review PR on the same two-window cadence, every other major is held 30 days for review. Security/CVE fixes bypass the schedule via the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block (0-day PR); a security major, like any major, opens for review rather than auto-merging.

pre-commit.description: Renovate ships the pre-commit manager DISABLED by default, so every .pre-commit-config.yaml rev in the org was frozen - a manual pre-commit autoupdate was the only thing that ever moved one. Enabled here so hook revs ride the same publisher-agnostic minor/patch auto-merge tier as everything else.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security/CVE remediation branches. minimumReleaseAge 0 + schedule 'at any time' surface the fix as a 0-day PR, bypassing the normal stabilization window. AUTOMERGE IS DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE so the decision falls to packageRules (deterministic and order-independent): a security minor/patch inherits the broad rule's automerge:true (fast auto-merge), while a security MAJOR inherits major-default automerge:false and opens for human review — a CVE fix that needs a breaking major is exactly when blind auto-merge is most dangerous. Setting automerge:true here would auto-merge security majors too, contradicting the majors-always-reviewed policy.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Bulk lock regeneration delegates version choice to the package manager, so Renovate cannot apply minimumReleaseAge and a stale renovate/stability-days status is expected rather than actionable. Disable that unsupported check only for lock maintenance. Renovate creates/updates lock-maintenance branches only in the Monday 05:00-08:59 or Thursday 13:00-16:59 America/New_York source windows, then directly automerges only during the Thursday 09:00-23:59 or Sunday 18:00-23:59 windows. Each window still begins more than 72 actual hours after the latest possible source-window update, including the spring DST transition, so the soak is unchanged. The Sunday window keeps its original 18:00 start for exactly that reason: the Thursday source window can end at 16:59 EST, and on the spring-forward Sunday 17:00 EDT is only 71h01m of real time later, which would shorten the soak. Thursday's window has no such constraint and starts at 09:00. The windows were widened from four hours to full evenings because Renovate itself performs the merge (platformAutomerge stays false) and a hosted run has to land INSIDE the window: a four-hour target was missed often enough that lock PRs routinely sat open for days and were merged by hand. The windows are now best-effort - the bot-pr-automerge-sweep.yml backstop in this repo enforces the same 72-hour age gate on its own hourly schedule and is what actually guarantees the merge. updateNotScheduled:false prevents an intervening head refresh. With platformAutomerge:false, Renovate honors this automergeSchedule and still requires green CI.

description: Disabled for Nix flakes ONLY (lockFileMaintenance stays ON for npm/terraform/python/etc.). Flake inputs (git-refs) move hourly, and lockFileMaintenance delegates to `nix flake update`, which resolves to absolute-latest and ignores minimumReleaseAge (Renovate docs: lockFileMaintenance does not support it). Enabled + automerged it looped create->automerge->recreate ~60 PRs/week on churny flake repos (nix-darwin, nix-ai), ignoring the two-window schedule. KEEP IT OFF.

SUPERSEDED 2026-08-05 — the whole `nix` MANAGER is now off too (see renovate-nix.json), so this setting is belt-and-braces rather than the operative control. flake.lock has exactly one writer: the _update-flake-lock.yml reusable workflow in this repo, which every nix repo calls via .github/workflows/deps-flake-lock.yml on a weekly schedule, on repository_dispatch, and on demand. It runs a bare `nix flake update` onto the single branch `chore/flake-lock`, so a repo never has more than one open flake PR.

WHY THE MANAGER COULD NOT COVER IT: Renovate updates an input when its REFERENCE changes. That works for DIGEST-TRACKED inputs (devenv, git-hooks, treefmt-nix) but is FALSE for CHANNEL-PINNED inputs such as github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-26.05-darwin — a channel branch's reference never changes, so there is nothing to diff and the locked rev freezes permanently. Measured 2026-07-28: nix-devenv/channels/flake.lock had been modified exactly once since creation 8 weeks earlier, nix-claude-code was 65 days stale and nix-home 58 days, all with Renovate running and the nix manager enabled.

SCHEDULE NOTE: the Thursday window is written `* 13-14 * * 4`, not `* 18 * * 4`, because the top-level timezone is America/New_York. The intended wall time is 18:00 UTC, which is 14:00 EDT and 13:00 EST — no single ET hour holds year-round, so the two-hour range covers both. Do not 'simplify' it to one hour.

customManagers.description: Renovate-annotated version pins in Nix files. HASH FIELDS ARE NOT UPDATED — only version strings. Each repo's fix-renovate-hashes.yml runs nix-update to fix adjacent hash = "sha256-..." fields after Renovate bumps a version. When adding a new fetchPypi/fetchurl package with a Renovate annotation, also add it to that repo's nix-update workflow and flake packages output.

Renovate-annotated version pins in GitHub Actions workflow shell blocks — release binaries downloaded by URL that the built-in github-actions manager (uses: refs only) never sees, e.g. the osv-scanner binary in dryvist/.github's _osv-scan.yml. Same annotation grammar as the .nix manager above, matching the shell assignment form VAR="value" on the line after the annotation.

description: Docker images pinned in Ansible role defaults as `<name>_image: "repo:tag"`. These live in plain YAML vars that no built-in Renovate manager scans, so image pins across ansible-proxmox-apps roles (prometheus_stack, netmon, qdrant_docker, ntfy_docker, mailpit_docker, unifi_metrics, seerr, ...) were untracked. Matched as the `docker` datasource so Renovate bumps the tag in place; image refs are self-describing (repo:tag) so no per-line `# renovate:` annotation is needed. Untagged refs (no colon) are not matched; local-only tags resolve to nothing and are skipped.

BOTH defaults layouts are matched, and the second pattern is not optional. A role may keep its defaults in one `defaults/main.yml` OR split them into a `defaults/main/` directory of topic-named files, which the per-file token budget pushes roles toward. A pattern matching only the file form silently drops every pin in a split role: no warning, no error, no dashboard entry — the role just stops being tracked the moment it is refactored, and the omission is invisible until someone reads a version by hand. Splitting a role is therefore a Renovate-affecting change: any new defaults layout needs a pattern here in the same change that introduces it, and nix/renovate-manager-coverage-selftest.py asserts both shapes stay matched.

Renovate-annotated version pins in Ansible role defaults (YAML). Mirrors the .nix annotation manager but for role defaults — binary version vars (e.g. traefik_version, object_storage_rustfs_version) interpolated into download URLs that no built-in manager scans. Only lines carrying an explicit `# renovate:` annotation are matched. Release checksums are fetched at install time (no hash field to update here), so unlike the .nix manager no companion hash-fixer workflow is needed. Matches the single `defaults/main.yml` and split `defaults/main/*.yml` layouts, plus `vars/`, `tasks/`, `templates/`, `inventory/`, `group_vars/`, `host_vars/`, `playbooks/` and `scripts/` — an annotated pin is just as untracked in any of those as in `defaults/`, and confining the manager to `defaults/` left every one of them invisible.

Neither matchString names the variable it expects, so both bind to whatever real (non-comment, non-blank) line comes first after the annotation — true before this change too. An annotation placed above the wrong line does not fail to match; it tracks the WRONG key's value under the annotated dep's name. Keep the annotation immediately (ignoring only blank/comment lines) above the pin it actually describes.

customManagers.description: Manage the Biome version pinned in each repo's biome.jsonc `$schema` URL. Every dryvist repo carries a scaffolded biome.jsonc, so this keeps @biomejs/biome current in lockstep with the schema URL. Moved here from renovate.json so it reaches every consumer through the shared preset instead of the deprecated renovate.json-as-preset fallback.

The `python-version:` field of actions/setup-python steps in GitHub Actions workflows. No built-in manager extracts this — pip_requirements/pep723/etc. all read dependency files, none read a workflow step input — so every repo's interpreter pin (3.9 through 3.14, inconsistent across repos) sat frozen. Matches `X.Y` or `X.Y.Z` — an earlier `X.Y`-only pattern captured just the PREFIX of a patch-pinned value (`3.12.4` -> currentValue `3.12`), so Renovate would have proposed `3.13.4`, a version that mixes a bumped minor with the original patch and was never actually released. A floating `"3.x"` pin has no discrete version to bump and is left alone. A `python-version: ${{ matrix.python }}` / matrix-list form (an array under a separate `python:` matrix key, not this field) is untracked, not mis-extracted — this manager only ever sees the literal field value.

Literal `node-version` fields in GitHub Actions setup-node steps. Keep this custom manager alongside the shared Renovate validator runtime pin so the validator's compatible Node release stays tracked.
The `RENOVATE_VERSION` environment pin used by the shared Renovate config validator. The workflow YAML environment field is outside built-in package managers, so track it through the npm datasource.

`pip install 'pkg==X.Y.Z'` pins inside a workflow `run:` step. The built-in `pip_requirements` manager only scans `requirements*.txt`/`.pip` files, never a shell command, so an inline install pin (e.g. `pip install 'check-jsonschema==0.37.2'`) is invisible to it. `matchStringsStrategy: recursive` finds each `pip install` (or `pip3 install`) invocation on a single line first, then re-scans that matched text for every `pkg==version` token in it — the shape needed when a line installs several pinned packages at once, not just the first. Unpinned packages and range constraints (`pkg>=X`) on the same line are not dependencies with a single currentValue and are left alone. `currentValue` excludes `*` and requires a trailing quote/whitespace/end boundary, so a wildcard pin (`'ansible-lint==25.*'`) fails to match rather than being truncated to `25.` and handed to pypi as a real (and wrong) currentValue — an earlier version of this pattern did exactly that. `pkg[extra]==X` (the `[proxy]`/`[docker]` extras syntax) and a backslash-continued multi-line `pip install \` block are both untracked, not mis-extracted: `depName`'s character class has no `[`/`]`, and the outer match is confined to a single line (`[^\n]*`).

description: Git-pinned Ansible collections/roles in requirements.yml. The built-in ansible-galaxy manager reads only `name` + `version` Galaxy pins; a `type: git` entry pinned to a 40-char commit SHA is invisible to it, so the pin never appears on the Dependency Dashboard and never gets a PR. Both real cases here are long-lived on purpose -- an immutable SHA used as a review gate, and an upstream-bug workaround on a fork -- which is exactly why they rot unnoticed: nothing ever proposes moving them.

Only lines carrying an explicit `# renovate:` annotation are matched, mirroring the role-defaults annotation manager above. The annotation supplies datasource/depName/currentValue (the branch the digest sits on) and the `version:` SHA below it is the currentDigest, which is the shape Renovate needs to propose a digest bump.

Upstream-release watch for a dependency deliberately pinned AWAY from upstream (a fork, a patched build, a vendored copy). Digest-tracking the fork answers 'did the fork move', never 'can we stop using the fork' -- so the workaround outlives its cause with nothing to say so.

Annotate with a datasource/depName pointing at UPSTREAM plus an `upstream-latest:` comment holding the newest upstream version known when the pin was written. Renovate bumps that comment when upstream publishes, turning 'the fix finally shipped' into a PR instead of a thing someone has to remember to check.

customManagers.description: Annotated SHA-pinned refs in YAML and env-style files. A `# renovate: datasource=github-tags depName=dryvist/<repo>` annotation on the line above a `key: "<40-hex commit SHA>"  # vX.Y.Z` pin (YAML) or a `KEY=<40-hex commit SHA>  # vX.Y.Z` pin (env files) tracks the trailing version comment as currentValue and the SHA as currentDigest, so the SHA and its comment move together. Comment-only lines may sit between the annotation and the pin. depName is any owner/repo the annotation names; nothing here is specific to one repository. The annotated-pin managers above skip 40-hex SHA values, which this manager owns.

packageRules.description: Disable all updates in gh-aw generated files — managed by gh-aw-pin-refresh workflow, not Renovate

Tag major updates with an additive `update:major` label (minor/patch are inferred by its absence). Gives the dryvist/ai-workflows dependency reviewer a deterministic, AI-independent 'is this a major?' gate so majors never auto-merge, and lets humans filter. addLabels is additive: it does not disturb scheduling, auto-merge, or the dep:review label. First-party dryvist/** majors are excluded: they auto-merge after green CI.

Major-version default, org-wide: hold non-trusted-vendor majors 30 days before a PR opens, and never auto-merge (human review required). The grace gives upstream ecosystems time to surface breaking-change regressions before we adopt them. Rules below are placed AFTER this one so their values win per-attribute (Renovate merges packageRule attributes by last-match wins): own-org restores immediate auto-merge for JacobPEvans/** majors (dryvist/** majors never auto-merge; see the dryvist/** rules); the trusted-orgs MAJOR rule shortens the hold to 3 days and opens a review PR (still no auto-merge — a trusted publisher is not proof of a compatible API); the trusted-orgs minor/patch rule auto-merges those (3-day stabilization, Fri ~15:00/Mon ~05:00 ET). Non-trusted-vendor majors match only this rule and stay held 30 days. CVE-driven bumps bypass the grace entirely via the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block (0 days, any time).

Publisher-agnostic non-major auto-merge (the broad tier). ANY package, ANY ecosystem: minor, patch, digest and pin updates auto-merge after a 3-day stabilization + green CI. DIGEST/PIN ARE IN THIS LIST DELIBERATELY: Renovate classes a SHA re-pin as updateType `digest` (and a first-time pin as `pin`/`pinDigest`), NOT as minor or patch, so while this rule read [minor, patch] every digest bump fell through to the default automerge:false and Renovate stamped `Automerge: Disabled by config` on the PR. Combined with the org-wide pinDigests:true rule below - which mandates that every external GitHub Action be SHA-pinned - that made digest bumps the single highest-volume PR class in the org AND the one class that could never self-merge, so each one waited on a human or an agent. A digest re-pin of an already-approved action at an already-approved version carries strictly less semantic risk than the patch bumps this rule already auto-merges. Majors are untouched: the major-default rule above still holds them 30 days at automerge:false. Trust tiers now gate ONLY majors and PR-creation cadence, never minor/patch — a non-major SemVer bump with green CI (the Merge Gate, plus the deterministic dependency-review supply-chain scan on public repos) is sufficient assurance, and a stale pin is drift to eliminate. Placed AFTER the major-default rule (majors do not match here) and BEFORE the own-org rule so first-party minor/patch keep their 0-day/any-time immediacy (Renovate is last-match-wins per attribute). PR creation is Fri ~15:00/Mon ~05:00 ET; merges flow continuously via automergeSchedule once the 3-day age + CI are satisfied, so a PR that turns green mid-week is not stalled to the next creation window (platformAutomerge stays false — see the top-level warning). This SUPERSEDES the former curated trusted-org minor/patch allowlist and the per-manager pre-commit / Terraform-provider / HuggingFace-PyPI / Python minor/patch carve-outs, all redundant once minor/patch is publisher-agnostic. Majors are unaffected: JacobPEvans majors auto-merge immediately (own-org rule), dryvist/** majors do too, except on automerge-manual repos, trusted-org majors open a 3-day review PR, all other majors are held 30 days — none auto-merge. Security/CVE fixes open a 0-day PR via the top-level vulnerabilityAlerts block.

Auto-merge own-org dependencies (JacobPEvans / JacobPEvans-personal) — immediate, all ecosystems, all update types including major. Placed AFTER the major-default rule so we restore immediate auto-merge for our own majors that the major-default rule would otherwise hold for 30 days. Also overrides the top-level two-window `schedule` with `at any time` so first-party changes propagate on merge, not on the Fri/Mon window — release-please cuts + auto-merges the release, and consumers pick it up here at 0-day. JacobPEvans-personal is the renamed legacy personal account (dryvist/JacobPEvans account split); JacobPEvans/** still resolves via redirect but the current owner is listed explicitly. The `https://github.com/<owner>/**` forms cover a git-refs customManager dependency (e.g. the requirements.yml annotation manager below): its packageName is the full clone URL it was annotated with, never the bare `owner/repo` form the other patterns match, so both forms are needed to treat a first-party git-ref pin as own-org.

Pin external GitHub Action refs to a full commit SHA (supply-chain hardening). Replaces the invalid top-level `pinGitHubActionDigests` key with Renovate's canonical per-manager `pinDigests`. Scoped to the `github-actions` manager, so it pins both `uses:` action refs AND any container/service images referenced in workflow jobs — a deliberate superset of the `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` preset (which only covers `uses:`). First-party refs (dryvist / JacobPEvans / JacobPEvans-personal) are exempted by the rule immediately below (Renovate is last-match-wins per attribute).
JacobPEvans and JacobPEvans-personal reusable workflows ride their floating major tag (@v1) and are not digest-pinned. dryvist/** refs are covered by the next rule.

dryvist/** GitHub Actions refs are pinned to a full 40-character commit SHA with the release tag in a trailing comment: uses: dryvist/<repo>/...@<sha> # vX.Y.Z. Renovate moves the SHA and the comment together.
dryvist/** patch updates, any package manager: auto-merge after green CI, no release-age hold, scheduled at any time.

dryvist/** minor updates, any package manager: auto-merge after green CI, no release-age hold, scheduled at any time. Repos whose automerge property is manual are excluded by the last rule in this list.

dryvist/** digest, pin and pinDigest updates, any package manager: Renovate does not auto-merge them; the bot-PR auto-merge sweep merges each once its head commit has soaked and checks are green. A digest update means a ref or a version comment moved without a release.
dryvist/** major updates, any package manager: auto-merge after green CI, scheduled at any time. Repos whose automerge property is manual are excluded by the last rule in this list.

Trusted-org MAJOR updates: shorten the major-default 30-day hold to 3 days and open a review PR, but do NOT auto-merge — a trusted publisher is not proof of a compatible API (breaking majors can pass shallow CI yet break runtime behavior, infra convergence, provider schemas, or CLI flags). Same curated allowlist as the minor/patch rule above. Labelled dep:review so humans can find them; Fri ~15:00/Mon ~05:00 ET visibility. Non-trusted majors are unaffected and stay in the 30-day hold.
GitHub releases use v-prefixed tags for custom Nix packages

The rule above strips the leading "v" from every github-releases tag it matches so a bare-pinned file (no "v" in currentValue) compares correctly. It has no way to tell that a v-prefixed pin (currentValue itself starts with "v", e.g. "v0.8.6") needs the opposite: extractVersion overwrites the datasource's release.version unconditionally, and the default versioning's getNewValue only restores a stripped prefix for the reverse case (bare currentValue, prefixed currentVersion), so a v-prefixed pin's write loses its own "v" every bump. A full-string capture is a no-op extraction — release.version is reassigned to itself — so the raw, still-prefixed tag reaches the write untouched.

Fri ~15:00 / Mon ~05:00 America/New_York schedule for all custom regex managers, except first-party (own-org) packageNames — those keep the own-org rule's `at any time` schedule (Renovate is last-match-wins per attribute, and this rule sits after the own-org rule in the array, so without the exclusion it would win back the two-window schedule for every first-party git-refs dep the annotation managers above track).
Disables the ansible-galaxy manager's github-tags/git-tags lookups; git-pinned collections are tracked by the git-pinned-collections custom.regex manager (git-refs) instead.
git-refs supplies no release timestamp; timestamp-optional lets minimumReleaseAge pass for git-refs updates instead of holding them indefinitely. Every other datasource still requires a timestamp.

Repos whose automerge custom property is manual (tofu-github config/automerge.yml: every ansible-* repo and nix-ai): Renovate never auto-merges there, and the org-automerge-manual ruleset requires a person's approval. Last rule so it overrides every automerge setting above.
